overview.description: Gnav is a Scandinavian elimination game from the Cuckoo family. Each round players hold one hidden piece, may stand or try to swap left, and try to avoid finishing with the lowest value.
overview.deck: Custom 42-piece Gnav pack (two of each rank/special piece)

history.origins: Gnav is a traditional round game played in Norway and in some parts of Denmark (for example on the island of Møn) as a family game on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve. It is closely related to the old Italian game Cuccù, the German Hexenspiel and the Swedish Byteskille; a variant known as Slabberjan is played in Zeeland in the Netherlands.
timeline: 18th Century: Becomes a popular Christmas game in Norway.
19th Century: Special wooden pieces ('brikker') become the standard equipment to allow hidden play under a table.
Present: Still played as a family tradition during holidays.
history.evolution: Core play stayed stable: one hidden piece, leftward swaps, and special top matadors that block or redirect swaps.
history.cultural: It is commonly played as a family holiday game and often uses small tokens or matches as lives.

setup.deck: 42 total pieces: two each of Gjok (cuckoo), Dragon, Katt, Hest, Hus, XII-XI-X-IX-VIII-VII-VI-V-IV-III-II-I, 0, Potte, Ugle, and Narr.
setup.equipment: Gnav card pack or wooden pawns, plus tokens or matches used as lives and a central pool.
setup.dealing: Dealer gives one hidden piece to each player; each player privately checks their own value.

rules.objective: Avoid ending the round with the lowest piece and preserve your tokens while other players are eliminated.
rules.gameplay: Play starts left of dealer and proceeds clockwise. On turn, a player either stands or tries to swap with the left neighbor. A normal neighbor must swap, but top five matadors change this. Cuckoo stops further swapping and triggers immediate reveal. Dragon and Katt refuse the swap and force the attacker to pay a token. Hest and Hus pass the attacker onward so they must try the next player instead. When play reaches dealer, dealer may exchange with the undealt stock with the same matador consequences; when a pass reaches dealer, draw replacement pieces until a non-pass value appears. At round end all reveal. Lowest value pays one token to pool; ties for lowest each pay.
keyRules: If dealt Narr (fool), you must signal it by knocking; at reveal both fool holder and next-lowest holder pay.
If two fools are in play, both fool holders pay and may sit out the next round.
Players who lose all tokens are eliminated; last remaining player wins the session.

strategy.basic: Stand on strong values and matadors; swap aggressively from low numbers and bottom specials.
strategy.intermediate: Track fool knocks and pass-chain effects from Hest and Hus to anticipate where dangerous pieces move.
strategy.advanced: Use seat position: when late in order, standing on mid values can be correct if several weak pieces are likely still right of you.
tips: Cuckoo can end the round early, so value volatility is higher before dealer acts.
Dragon and Katt penalties can be as costly as losing low-card reveal; account for both risks.

difficulty.hard: Tracks positional risk, fool information, and elimination pressure to optimize expected token loss.

synthesis.shortDescription: A one-piece elimination game where players attempt leftward swaps under matador constraints and pay tokens when caught with the lowest reveal.

prompts.human: Gnav round: check your hidden piece, decide whether to stand or swap left, and manage matador outcomes to avoid finishing lowest.
prompts.ai: Play Gnav with exact matador responses, fool side-rules, and token-elimination accounting. Stop swap loop immediately when Cuckoo appears.

scoring.description: At reveal, the lowest piece holder pays one token to the pool. Ties for lowest each pay. Fool side-rules can require additional payer(s).
scoring.winCondition: Last player with at least one token remaining wins the session.

penalties.dragon_or_katt_block: Attacker pays one token immediately when blocked by Dragon or Katt.
penalties.fool_rule: Fool holder and next-lowest holder both pay at reveal.

scoring.splitRules: If multiple players tie for lowest relevant value, each tied player pays one token.

nullReasons.targetScore: Gnav is elimination-based and not played to a numeric target score.
nullReasons.scoringDirection: Higher or lower aggregate points are not tracked; only token survival matters.
